title: Sampling macrofungi using fixed-sized plots
author: Gregory M. Mueller
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.z2xf8fn

steps.title: Select and establish the plot area
steps.instruction: Select a representative area within the site for the permanent plot that optimizes habitat diversity (e.g., grasslands, open woodlands, dense forest) and is as homogenous and accessible as possible while avoiding edge effects.

steps.title: Lay out transects
steps.instruction: Establish 10 transects, each 100 m long, within the plot.

substeps.instruction: Lay transects parallel to one another at 10-m intervals, or end-to-end if the area shape requires it.
Mark transects every 5 m with a flag or stake.
Assign each transect a unique letter and number flags sequentially (e.g., A1-A20; B1-B20; ...; J1-J20).

steps.title: Delineate circular subplots
steps.instruction: Use a 1.262 m rope and a plastic pipe or wooden pole to circumscribe 5-m² circular subplots around each flag.

substeps.instruction: Create 20 subplots per transect for a total of 200 subplots (1000 m² or 0.1 ha per plot).
Avoid walking in or unnecessarily disturbing the subplots.

steps.title: Collect and process macrofungi
steps.instruction: Collect all macrofungi occurring within each subplot and document their origin.

substeps.instruction: Label specimens with the transect letter and subplot number.
Place specimens in an appropriate bag or container.
Note the substratum (soil, leaf litter, wood) for each specimen.
Transport specimens to the field station at the end of the collecting day for sorting, describing, photographing, and drying.
